list.title: Data sources
list.description: Where exposures and metric events are read from. The built-in store works out of the box; connect BigQuery, Snowflake, ClickHouse or Postgres to use your warehouse.
list.warehouseHint: Already have events in a warehouse, like a GA4 or Segment export? Connect it and furca reads exposures and metrics straight from your tables with SQL you control. Templates are included.

new.title: Connect a warehouse
new.description: Analyze experiments with exposures and events already in your warehouse. Pick where they live.
new.createdToastDescription: Test the connection to check access and the exposure query.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.description: Metrics that read their events from this source.
metrics.empty: No metrics use this source yet. <link>Create a metric</link> and pick it as the data source.

builtin.description: Always on, nothing to configure. Exposures and events sent by the SDK are stored in D1 and analyzed in the Worker.

steps.exposures: When a user is bucketed into a running experiment, the SDK records which variation they saw. Repeats are de-duplicated per user and variation, and bot traffic is dropped.
steps.events: <c>furca.track(name, value?)</c> records an event. Metrics count them, or sum their value (e.g. revenue).
steps.storage: The SDK batches both to <endpoint/> and they're written to this deployment's D1 database, in your Cloudflare account.

builtin.ingestionDescription: Hourly volume in {{environment}}. Switch environments in the sidebar.
builtin.eventNamesDescription: Distinct events received in {{environment}} over the last 30 days, most frequent first.
builtin.eventNamesEmpty: No events yet. Call <c>furca.track("purchase")</c> from your app; <link>the quickstart</link> has the setup for each runtime.

test.title: Connection test
test.description: Authenticates with the stored key and dry-runs the exposure query. Dry runs are free and read no data.
test.notTested: Not tested since this page opened.
test.scan: The exposure query would scan <bytes>{{bytes}}</bytes> per analysis.
test.descriptionLimit0: Authenticates with the stored credentials and runs the exposure query with LIMIT 0, which compiles it without reading rows.

noSecret.bigquery: Add a service account key below, then test.
noSecret.snowflake: Add the user's private key below, then test.
noSecret.clickhouse: Add the password below, then test.
noSecret.postgres: Add the password below, then test.

delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
delete.body: The stored credentials are erased. This can't be undone.
delete.inUse_one: {{count}} metric reads from this source (archived ones included). Point it at another source first; a source in use can't be deleted.
delete.inUse_other: {{count}} metrics read from this source (archived ones included). Point them at another source first; a source in use can't be deleted.

key.title: Service account key
key.dropLabel: Drop a service account JSON key
key.placeholder: Paste the JSON key, or drop the .json file here
key.needsRoles: The service account needs BigQuery Job User and BigQuery Data Viewer on the project. Paste the key to get the exact commands.
key.notServiceAccount: This isn't a service account key. In Google Cloud, open IAM → Service accounts → Keys → Add key → JSON.
key.invalidJson: This isn't valid JSON. Paste the whole key file, including the braces.

sql.title: Exposure query
sql.description: Tells furca who saw which variation. Used when experiments analyze this source instead of the SDK's built-in exposures.
sql.help: One row per exposure event (don't de-duplicate; furca splits phases by time) with columns <c>user_id</c> {{text}}, <c>timestamp</c> {{time}}, <c>experiment_key</c> {{text}}, <c>variation_key</c> {{text}}. Optionally filter with <c>@experiment_key</c>, <c>@start_ms</c> and <c>@end_ms</c> (epoch ms), e.g. to prune partitions.
sql.label: {{warehouse}} SQL

errors.name: Name the data source
errors.projectId: Enter the Google Cloud project id
errors.location: Enter the dataset location, e.g. US
errors.credentials: Paste or drop the service account key
errors.sql: Write the exposure query, or start from a template
errors.account: Enter only the account identifier, e.g. myorg-myaccount
errors.url: Enter an https:// URL without a user name or password
errors.host: Enter only the host name, e.g. db.example.com

form.secretDescription: Stored encrypted with this deployment's <c>ENCRYPTION_KEY</c> and never shown again. furca only runs read queries.
form.secretStored: {{secret}} is stored for this data source.

privateKey.title: Private key
privateKey.placeholder: Paste the unencrypted PKCS#8 private key, or drop the .p8 file here
privateKey.required: Paste or drop the user's private key
privateKey.encrypted: Encrypted keys aren't supported. Create the key with -nocrypt, or decrypt it with openssl pkcs8.
privateKey.pkcs1: This is a PKCS#1 key. Convert it with: openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -nocrypt -in key.pem -out rsa_key.p8
privateKey.invalid: This isn't a private key. It starts with -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----.
privateKey.register: Register its public key on the Snowflake user (run as a user administrator):
privateKey.howTo: No key yet? Create one, then paste rsa_key.p8 here to get the ALTER USER statement.

access.snowflake: The user's role needs USAGE on the warehouse, database and schema, and SELECT on the tables your SQL reads.
access.clickhouse: Use a user that can only SELECT the tables your SQL reads (readonly users work).
access.postgres: Use a user that can only SELECT the tables your SQL reads. The database must accept connections from the internet (Cloudflare Workers).

snowflake.role: Optional. Empty uses the user's default role.

postgres.host: Host name only, without postgres:// or a path.

types.bigquery: Google's warehouse. Works with GA4 and Segment exports; free dry runs check queries before they run.
types.snowflake: Key-pair authentication over the SQL API. Reads exposures and events from your Snowflake tables.
types.clickhouse: Self-hosted or ClickHouse Cloud, over the HTTPS interface.
types.postgres: Any PostgreSQL 12+ reachable from the internet: Amazon RDS / Aurora, Cloud SQL, Neon, Supabase and more.
